reviewer: Grok (Mini, 2026-09-19): clause-by-clause vs locked PG 10 / Khazarzar Cesti Greek; sections 42-45 new (book 2); 1-41 re-read against the same lock

scope_review.notes: Expanded tip: Cesti book 7 through colophon, plus book 2.1–2.8. Author Sextus Julius Africanus. PG 10 via Khazarzar. Not the letters. Remainder of book 2 and the book-7 appendix held. No Scripture quotations in this slice.

reviews.notes: Pinax of Cesti book 7 kept: twenty heads from ὁπλίσεως through Ἐπισφράγισμα περὶ βέλους. Blank numeral before Ἵππου τιθασία treated as item 6 by order. Negation kept on μὴ χρεμετίσαι and μὴ πτοεῖσθαι. No Scripture.

Proem: Κατὰ λόγον ἢ νόμον ἢ εἱμαρμένην ἢ τύχην four-way kept (reason/law/fate/chance). ἐκβάσεις births-destructions alterations-healings. First-person κατὰ τὸ ἐμαυτοῦ μέτριον κατώρθωται kept. No Scripture.

On arming opening through Macedonian successors. μηδέπω Persians not-yet beaten by Romans. πλήθους...λόγος οὐδὲ εἷς negation kept. Heavy panoply listed. Bracketed ὅπη δεῖ ἐλλεβοροστρῶσαι left unrendered. No Scripture.

On arming remainder. πίλῳ Λακωνικῷ free faces; Alexander ξυρεῖσθαι τοὺς πώγωνας and the beard-as-grip saying. Roman kit: single-material helmet to shoulder-blades, chain thorax, one greave, long σπάθη, θυρεὸς. πλινθίῳ brick-formation; knee-tiling against Parthian missiles. Ῥωμαῖος καθ' αὑτὸν οὐδείς negation kept. No Scripture.

Closes 7.1. Sling-shots crush the helmet; neck-iron blocks ducking. Ten javelins on one kill; small κοντοί vs horsemen. Counterfactual: Greek thorax+helmet+longer pike+solo fighting+run inside missiles → barbarian would not hold out (οὐκ ἂν...ἀρκέσειε). No Scripture.

Opens 7.2. οὐδὲ ποιητέον...κυρίαν τὴν τύχην: fortune not mistress. Pan at Marathon; Themistocles lie vs Xerxes; Leonidas equaled by Gates narrowness; Phocians fled the laurel crown. Hidden arts, Carthaginian law judging γνώμη not τύχη. Theriac vs poisoned missiles. No Scripture.
Starve barbarians (seasonal army). Air and water as allies. Pentagon αʹ conceals animals for last-day bread; lock lacuna after κίνδυνος. Pyrrhus consumed though having the advantage. No Scripture.

Unsuspected carrying / feigned flight. Plot migrates house-city-army-nation. Plotting kindness: release fed captives. Second pentagon (turned/upright gamma) for watering-place poison. Myrtle-spurge vs lakes. East barbarians not unlearned. No Scripture.

Φαρισαῖοι kept as print for the lime-wine ambush. τίτανος = quenched lime. Thrissos + lion-snake in third pentagon; Syrian βαθανηραθὰν in lock brackets. Air-exhalation examples: horse, man, bird. Themistocles snatches sleep. No Scripture quotation.

Closes 7.2. Night infantry + trumpeter-horsemen: either kill careless watches or throw πανικόν. Noise > wound. Next days refuse battle; same men kept sleepless. αὐτοβοεὶ...τεθηλυμμένους: take them at first shout, made womanish by sleeplessness. No Scripture.

7.3 Athletic. Cock-stones in bellies of noble cocks as victory-helpers; true color black. Winner-cock eaten whole, bones kept, then fire-purified. ὁ Νεοκλέους = Themistocles; cock-fights after Median victory. No Scripture.

7.4 Cutting. δειλοί toward necessary iron treatments; fear of ἰάσεως ἀλγηδών vs untreated βλάβος. Light hand, sharp ἀκμή; bluntness painful. ἐπιπασάτω τῇ πλίνθῳ: sprinkle the pentagon-4 coded drug. No Scripture.
7.5 Iron wound. ἀλεῖψαι the wounding iron then ἐπικροῦσαι it to the wound; spit while saying τὰ τὰ thrice; pentagon εʹ Roman formula. Pain ceases; ἰατρῶν παῖδες treat the wound. No Scripture.

7.6 Horse taming. Rare genuine virtue; vices listed. Colt-tamer arts: scant food, gelding, muzzles, λύκοις = wolf-bits not wolves. Untameable adult vice; hoof writing at 16th-day moon, pentagon numeral blank. No Scripture.

7.7 Not-neigh. Aristomenes with a mare exposed a Spartan ambush; later silenced his own horses by a station of Spartan mares. Parthians lead horses silent. Tail bound with well-twisted sinew above the hair: pain keeps θυμός and speed, ἴσχει only the voice. No Scripture.

7.8 Cataract. Homer's speaking horses as ἵππειον μάθημα, not daimons; living horses see daimons at τρίοδοι. ἑτερόμματοι excel. Abstain from Aphrodisia. Bacchic plant = ivy ointment, skip-day cycle, until accustomed prophetic sight. Cough recipe deferred ἔνδον. No Scripture.
7.9 Not-startle. Tail of a living θηρίον attached to the right ear; pentagon ζʹ (hypate meson, sigma+sigma) conceals the beast. No Scripture.

7.10 Speed. Daggered λύκος ἀντιπαθὲς clause left corrupt, word-for-word. Wolf-feet prized; hung ἀστράγαλος checks a runner. Living wolf κυνόδοντες in περιδεραίοις: unsuspected help + contest ornament. Lead horse enough for the four-horse team. No Scripture.

7.11 Horse-frightener opening. Sybarite horses dance to the aulos; insulted piper delivers them to Croton. Taraxippos Poseidon. Drug in πυουλκοί (pentagon ηʹ, rho + inverted sigma) squeezed into horses' breaths; riders fall, fettered by their own θώρακες. No Scripture.

Closes 7.11. Sea-turtle bile drops a horse; saffron+myrrh+lily raises it. καρπάσου juice more death-dealing; phalangia, salamander, ivy-tear, storax, menstrual-rag smoke. Dercyllidas: πλινθίον back-to-back, pits under shield vs cavalry. No Scripture.

Opens 7.12. Remedy against pack-animal destruction (veterinary). Celery/linseed/fenugreek/vetch cakes; wolf-steaks; rotting dog-head smoke. Roman many-ingredient drench starts; lock lacuna after white pepper unrestored. πίτυι as bran. No Scripture.

Closes 7.12. Fivefold continuation of the Roman drench: left nostril through the horn; full mix to adult mules, half to horses. Hulled lentil for cough; lice/bedbugs or wet pitch for orthopnoea. No Scripture.
7.13 Kicking mule. Roman voice already given in 7.6. Box-seed + caltrops boiled in wine; months numeral blank in the lock. No Scripture.

7.14 Military hunting. Lion taken by timing/art/engine not force. Infantry circle, shields tiled like κέραμοι, torches for spears; downhill galeagra with a kid; kataphracts behind with dry hides. Other manners elsewhere, not supplied. No Scripture.
Opens 7.15. Euclid I bisection theorem on right triangle ABΓ; dioptra at I, marks A and Υ; IΥ bisected at K. ζεῦγμα is the bridging-span; ἑλέπολις siege-towers. No Scripture.
Closes 7.15. Parallels give river width (I–Ρ, subtract Ρ–Φ). Same-bank rod+gnomon: BΓ:ΓΔ = AB:EΔ. Wall height on λυχνία pole, ἔξω βέλους. QED BA. No Scripture.

7.16 Theft of sound. Mauretanians: long sight from light air and no salt/hot; sleeping-wood and a pit for night hearing. Gaulish brigands. Deep well + cloak steals camp talk. Higher air full of sound. No Scripture.

Opens 7.17. Poets put Zeus to sleep (Hera+Sleep; Greeks breathe / Heracles harmed). Sleep stills rivers. Il. 10.98 quote; Rhesus betrayed by toil and sleep. Wine-and-flight night kill. Silenus/satyr bound sleeping. Membrane-winged milk-fed head-amulet. Name held for pentagon. Homeric, not Scripture.

Closes 7.17. Live-wing scraper-scoop for drink; head sewn to pillow. Pasithea marriage; cestus from Aphrodite (Il. 14). Lock Ἥρατούτου crux. Pentagon θʹ, Lydian enharmonic meson, π + reversed ς. Animal name not supplied. No Scripture.
Opens 7.18. Elephant as walking wall/portable phalanx; tusks, trunk-javelins, towers. Do not station cavalry; trumpets blunt the hiss; peltasts and fire-arrows at the towers. No Scripture.
Closes 7.18. Wounded beast turns on friends. Better not to close; iron caltrops take it by its own weight. Living captive more honorable than a general's shield. No Scripture.

Opens 7.19. Farming useful even in war. Not all countries bear all things. Boil-down wine (fire midwifed Dionysus). Zython, kamon, kerbesia, sikera. Fig-sea-licorice wine; winter vinegar from the same marc. Lock διαψιλῆ as δαψιλῆ. No Scripture.

Continues 7.19. Vinegar without spending the wine (grape-stone + marc). Pine-cone vinegar; lock cotylae numeral blank. Iberian oil with Roman fecula; Istrian almond; mastic chopped with a wooden pestle. No Scripture.
Continues 7.19 through garum. Terebinth like mastic; nitre brightens dirty oil; Spanum from Sidetic; suet oil with lock lacuna in the brine measure; Lydian garum and named soccius. No Scripture.
Closes 7.19 recipes. Ten xestai of abdomia, Libyan stagmas called phriton, Cretan hyssop, Roman orbiclatum apple, sixteen cotylai honey, fig-branch boil three days. No Scripture.
Opens 7.20 seal of the missile. Relay of ≤10 archers counted as one continuous flight: 6000 plethra/hour = 1000 stades; 24h + 1000 leisure = 25000 at equinox. No Scripture.

Closes book 7. Syrmos Scythian, Bardesanes Parthian, Mannos son of Abgar at Edessa (bear's eyes; shield-portrait; arrow catching arrow). Colophon Ἰουλίου Ἀφρικανοῦ Κεστὸς ζʹ. Appendix and book-2 pinax held. No Scripture.
Opens Cesti 2.1. ζηλωτός = enviable, not Zealot. Wine from Theban opium + henbane + dirt of a donkey's right ear puts drinkers to sleep three days; vinegar on the nostrils wakes them. No Scripture.
Cesti 2.2. Hellebore farming in enemy fields (same ruse as 7.2 vs Alans). Salt sown and ploughed in ruins fields a long time. No Scripture.
Cesti 2.3. Stingray sting in the stem dries every tree except apple. Quintilii: bean-husks at the roots. Africanus prefers cutting those grown for beauty. No Scripture.
Cesti 2.4. Neptunianus Physica: wolf right-fore ankle-bone stops a four-horse team; slingers throw them into the enemy horse. No Scripture.
Cesti 2.5. Scythian τοξικόν. Palisade spurge (τιθύμαλλος χαρακίτης) boiled in a new earthen vessel; sap as salve. Ancients add viper/asp/salamander. Africanus will not vouch the making. No Scripture.
Cesti 2.6. Little meals often; rue and wild mallow in turned wine; wormwood-wine and squill-wine/vinegar; marsh-wine; thin kiln-bread; boil sick water to a tenth. No Scripture.
Cesti 2.7. Fasting bolus: 20 rue leaves, 2 dried figs, equal walnuts, salt. Fuller: fatty figs, bright walnuts, dry rue, ripe juniper, Lemnian seal, Pontic-nut balls daily. No Scripture.
Cesti 2.8. Great iron cut glued without suture by the edible bulb pounded on. No Scripture.
